evidence.scope: Finite register traces and two derivations conditional on the stated algebraic laws. No general compiler-correctness theorem is machine-verified.

scope: All examples pass syntax round trips. Type-specific or semantic checks run only where individually declared; schematic type/logical data is syntax-only. The finite NatForm program is executed on its recorded examples, explicitly T-typed products are recomputed without promotion, and two rational approximation/error pairs are checked by endpoint or residual arithmetic. The G-to-L introduction examples check finite rational common-subsequence samples, sign branches, retained label indices, nonadditivity, one rational precision request, and explicit rejections; their general theorems remain written proofs. The H/decimal examples separately check finite recurrence traces against closed formulas, the specified Psi rule, exact repeating-decimal rational values, common finite decimal-prefix bounds for distinct labels, and concrete malformed or false claims. The pi examples check the named rule and version, two recurrence steps, finite strict membership witnesses, four prescribed rational brackets, both locatedness branches, and five malformed claims. Large endpoints use canonical rational-text certificate fields. The general exact-cut laws, correspondence with ordinary pi, and arbitrary exact equality are not machine-verified. No infinite geometric intersection or general volume theorem is machine-verified here. Decoded existing proof bundles are rechecked in their original kernels.
